chapters.title: Kitabu cha Wageni
chapters.body: A small AI guestbook for Noor, who runs coffee tours on her family farm in the Tanzanian highlands. Guests write in their own language; Noor hears it in Swahili.

chapters.title: A three-step guide
chapters.body: Opens by itself the first time. The whole app is one home screen; everything else is one tap away.

chapters.title: Try one example
chapters.body: An invented English-speaking guest. On the phone, the AI splits the feedback into sentences, matches each to a fixed list of 10 topics, and reads the mood.

chapters.title: The home screen
chapters.body: What guests said, in two lines, and the four things Noor does: add feedback, hand the phone to a guest, thank guests, see next week.

chapters.title: Noor’s phone shows it in Swahili
chapters.body: The interface follows the phone’s language. The summary is built from human-written Swahili sentences; the AI only fills in counts and topic names. “Sikiliza” reads it aloud.

chapters.title: Details: what guests said
chapters.body: Each topic keeps the guests’ own words. Anything the AI is unsure about is marked “Check” for a person to look at.

chapters.title: Thank the guest in their language
chapters.body: A human-written message in the guest’s language, with its meaning underneath. Noor sends it herself, and only if the guest agreed.

chapters.title: Hand the phone to a guest
chapters.body: The visitor screen speaks 8 languages. Giulia writes in Italian, ticks that she would buy coffee, and agrees to be contacted.

chapters.title: Analysed on the phone
chapters.body: Italian → English with a translation model on the phone (about 130 MB, downloaded once), then topics and mood. The feedback never leaves the phone.

chapters.title: Two guests now
chapters.body: Giulia’s wish to buy coffee is counted under products, so Noor (and, if she agrees, the tour company) can see the demand.

chapters.title: A photo of the paper guestbook
chapters.body: Lukas wrote in German in box A (what he liked). The text reader on the phone reads the photo; words it is unsure of are shown in yellow for the helper to fix.

chapters.title: Results to check
chapters.body: Each sentence shows the original, the English, a topic and a mood. A person can correct any label or press “OK”.

chapters.title: A voice message
chapters.body: Sophie left a voice message in French. Whisper (about 77 MB, on the phone) writes it down and translates it to English.

chapters.title: Four guests, four languages
chapters.body: What guests loved, what to improve, and what they wanted to buy. At the bottom: an anonymous report for the tour company, shared only if Noor agrees.

chapters.title: The tour company sends a booking
chapters.body: The app writes a short Swahili SMS for Noor’s basic phone; the company sends it from its own phone. No internet needed on Noor’s side.

chapters.title: Next week, and the languages to prepare
chapters.body: Polish guests are booked in 3 days, so the app asks to download Polish while the helper has Wi-Fi. Rare languages can be deleted afterwards.

chapters.title: Language packs on the phone
chapters.body: Swahili and English are built in. The 3 most common guest languages stay; others are downloaded before a visit and can be deleted afterwards.
